name: Cow milk, pasteurized, vitamin D added, 3.25% fat (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Cow milk, pasteurized, vitamin D added, 3.25% fat [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered (capped at 250).

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: MANUAL, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 746782 — Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D (SR Legacy)
PMID 1958838 — Variability of orotic acid concentration in cow's milk (mean 0.618 mmol/L)
Agrarforschung Schweiz 2008 — Orotic acid content in cow's, ewe's and goat's milk (6.3-7.6 mg/100g)
PMID 12237966 — Relationship between citrate and ketone bodies in cow's milk
Fox, Uniacke-Lowe, McSweeney & O'Mahony, Dairy Chemistry and Biochemistry (citrate 8-11 mmol/L; free sugars; chloride; myo-inositol; carnitine)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy source is LACTOSE (~4.8 g/100g, ~140 mM); the key growth-relevant organic acid CITRATE (~8.9 mM, ~1.7 g/L) and milk-specific OROTIC acid were absent from the FooDB profile and were added. Fresh pasteurized milk has only trace lactate (rises on souring). Cholesterol is retained (genuine animal-food lipid, unlike the plant-food rule). Removed heavy-metal/contaminant elements (arsenate, cadmium, aluminium, rubidium, boron, nickel) and implausible/mislabeled FooDB entries (D-g
curation_added: citric acid (0.17 g/100g — principal milk organic acid, was absent)
orotic acid (7 mg/100g — milk-specific pyrimidine acid)
riboflavin/B2 (0.169 mg — major milk vitamin, was absent)
butyric (4:0), myristic (14:0), palmitic (16:0), stearic (18:0), oleic (18:1), linoleic (18:2), alpha-linolenic (18:3) fatty acids

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
